data.component: primary-dns rate limiter (ratelimit: 20 q/s per /24) on dns1.lan, with gw.lan's unbound private-address filtering defeating the fallback
data.cause: The whole LAN shares one rate-limit bucket on dns1.lan (ratelimit: 20 q/s at /24 granularity), and when brief bursts exceed it — logged repeatedly through the day — queries are dropped; because the second server (gw.lan) filters the very private address that .lan names resolve to (private-address: 10.0.0.0/8 rebinding protection applied to answers forwarded from dns1), the client's fallback gets an empty NOERROR instead of an address, so getaddrinfo fails with ENOTFOUND until the burst passes and the alert self-clears.
evidence: mon.lan /etc/resolv.conf lists nameserver 10.20.0.3 then 10.20.0.1 — clients use dns1 first, gw as fallback.
dig @10.20.0.3 nas.lan on mon.lan returns 10.20.0.50 with TTL only 10 seconds — the short TTL makes every client re-query often, inflating query volume into one bucket.
dns1.lan /opt/primary-dns/config.yaml sets ratelimit: 20 with ratelimit_subnet_len_ipv4: 24, and rewrites *.lan/nas.lan to 10.20.0.50.

journalctl -u primary-dns on dns1.lan shows several episodes per day, e.g. 'ratelimit: 10.20.0.0/24 exceeded 20 q/s, dropping 23 queries' at 02:14 followed by 'back under limit' within ~1 second to 30 seconds — matching alerts that clear within a minute or two.
dig @10.20.0.1 nas.lan on mon.lan returns status NOERROR with ANSWER: 0 (empty answer, MSG SIZE 36) — the backup server never yields an address for local names.

gw.lan /var/unbound/unbound.conf contains 'private-address: 10.0.0.0/8' (DNS rebinding protection) while forwarding zone 'lan.' to 10.20.0.3 — so the forwarded private answer is filtered out, producing the empty NOERROR; internet names don't resolve to private addresses, which is why they are unaffected.
data.recommendation: Raise or remove the rate limit on dns1.lan's primary-dns (e.g. increase ratelimit well above normal burst levels or exempt the rewritten .lan answers), and ideally lengthen the 10-second TTL on the .lan rewrite to cut query volume. Also fix gw.lan's unbound config so rebinding protection doesn't discard answers from the forwarded lan. zone (e.g. serve the lan. zone locally there or exempt it from private-address filtering), so the second server can actually serve as a fallback. No reboot needed; a config reload suffices.
